repository.name: @webex/byods
repository.purpose: Published Node.js SDK for Webex Bring Your Own Data Source (BYoDS). One BYODS instance, built from a Service App client ID, client secret, and organization ID, obtains a Service App token pair from a personal access token or refresh token, keeps it in a caller-replaceable TokenStorageAdapter (one in-memory slot by default), and refreshes the access token when an expired one is read. Its data source client creates, reads, lists, updates, and deletes Webex /dataSources records with that token and can renew a data source JWS on a jittered timer; verifyJWSToken checks a JWS against the Webex identity broker key set and resolves a validity result. BYODS_ENVIRONMENT selects production or integration hosts at construction.

public_interfaces.name: @webex/byods package exports
entrypoints: import {BYODS, TokenManager, BaseClient, DataSourceClient, LOGGER, InMemoryTokenStorageAdapter} from '@webex/byods'
public_interfaces.audience: Node.js data source providers; in this workspace the private sample byods-demo-server, which imports the source path
public_interfaces.notes: Type exports: TokenStorageAdapter, SDKConfig, ServiceAppToken. package.json main names dist/module/index.js, which no script writes; build:src writes dist/index.js and dist/types (src/docs/README.md MOD-020).

public_interfaces.name: BYODS facade
public_interfaces.notes: BYODS_ENVIRONMENT=integration selects integration hosts at construction; any other value selects production. verifyJWSToken resolves a result object and never rejects.

public_interfaces.name: Token manager and storage adapter
public_interfaces.notes: One organization and one token slot per instance; an expired access token is refreshed when read. A custom TokenStorageAdapter implements setToken, getToken, deleteToken and returns Date expiry values.

public_interfaces.name: Data source client
public_interfaces.notes: A failed renewal tick ends the host process through an unhandled rejection, and the default nonce generator always fails on Node.js 22.14; always pass a nonce generator (src/docs/README.md MOD-016, MOD-017).

public_interfaces.name: package scripts
public_interfaces.notes: Run from packages/byods, or as yarn workspace @webex/byods followed by the script name from the workspace root. Yarn 3 does not run prebuild automatically.

evidence_rules.requirement: Ground every behavioral claim in source or test evidence; mark probe-only behavior as such.

negative_guidance.rule: Do not call scheduleJWSTokenRefresh without a nonce generator.
negative_guidance.why: The default generator throws on its first tick and the failure ends the process (src/docs/README.md MOD-016, MOD-017).

negative_guidance.rule: Do not let caller headers override the data source bearer token.
negative_guidance.why: Requests must act only as the configured Service App (src/docs/README.md INV-001).

negative_guidance.rule: Do not log token values or the client secret.
negative_guidance.why: Log lines go to the host console; current log calls carry no secret.

negative_guidance.rule: Do not treat README.md as the package API.
negative_guidance.why: It omits renewal failure handling and the entry-field gap. See docs/adr/0001-retain-product-readme.md.

negative_guidance.rule: Do not lower or bypass the jest.config.js coverage threshold.
negative_guidance.why: test:unit enforces it locally and in the pull-request workflow.

high.expectation: Source and unit test evidence both support the change, for example token refresh, header precedence, and environment selection.

medium.expectation: Only source or probe evidence exists, for example renewal tick failure, the default nonce generator, and the entry fields. Pin current behavior with a characterization test before modifying.

low.expectation: Neither source nor tests settle the question, for example Webex server behavior on reused refresh tokens. Stop and report the gap.
